architecture.A1_context: M01-S2 HOST definition codec/create/save/adopt; existing WORK domain accepted. UI/native/session ownership in S3.
architecture.A2_hexagonal: UI/native picker → Tauri → DispatchHost → HOST usecases → WORK; HOST → FileSystemPort(read)/FileCommitPort(write) ← Windows adapter.
architecture.A3_module_dependency: src-tauri → HOST → WORK + PORTS; ADAPTERS → PORTS + existing SPEC hash. No HOST std::fs, WORK serde, or UI adapter call.
architecture.A4_responsibility: WORK owns typed content rules; HOST owns mapping/orchestration; DispatchHost owns live binding/draft/peer projection; adapter owns OS handles/scratch.
architecture.A6_output_ports: Existing FileSystemPort read/exists/is_file; FileCommitPort exclusive create/acquire; lease read_current/replace_checked. No new Port.
architecture.A7_driving: Tests, then authorized S3 caller; no new global service.
architecture.A8_driven: Existing Windows IO adapter; test-only commit doubles backed by same fixture FS.
architecture.A9_direction: Adapters implement inward Ports; HOST maps DTO, Domain does not serialize.
architecture.A10_ownership: S2 returns immutable proof/binding, never registers active project or UUID. Caller must recheck current owner/session before applying returned binding.
architecture.A11_mutation: Only save requests writes through commit Port. No write_atomic/create_dir_all/remove_file in new store/create path; no source mutation.
architecture.A12_transaction: Root/metadata/definition/preferences are ordered steps, each formal file its own IO transaction. Definition first, prefs second. Later failure never rolls back a committed definition.
architecture.A13_external: Current IO local-scope accepted on Windows10; Windows11/reparse/8.3 remain separate. Existing read ports read whole files: codec cap is post-read, not bounded OS allocation. No universal CAS/power-loss promise.

RawDefinitionDigest.rule: Exact disk bytes, not reserialized content; separate from logical revision.

DefinitionAuthorityContext.rule: S3 authenticates against its own live owner. Nonempty strings/UI checkbox are NOT authorization. S2 has no window permission service.

OpenDefinitionClaim.rule: Supplied from serialized DispatchHost owner snapshot, not a new S2 registry. S3 revalidates before installing returned binding.

DefinitionLocation.rule: Canonicalization/authorization is outer-native responsibility; IO still validates target. UI-provided root is not authority.

DefinitionBaseline.rule: Absent requires missing target; never means overwrite approval.

PreparedPreferencePlan.rule: Prepare/validate before any directory creation. Only NewProject may write selected preferences. Captured import source is never a write target; no source path in portable definition.

DefinitionBinding.kind: public type, private fields; no Serialize/Deserialize
DefinitionBinding.rule: Only normal constructor bind_definition. Existing/adopt require Skip. Immutable caller-owned value; S2 returns next binding proposal, never installs it.

DefinitionOpenView.rule: Legacy iff definition truly NotFound, no auto ID/write. Saved data does not authorize generation.

DefinitionCommitProof.rule: Only after verified IO receipt; captured revision, not a later edited snapshot.

OwnedCreationArtifact.rule: Only successful exclusive create/receipt. IO scratch/recovery paths are not HOST cleanup ownership.

CreationProgress.rule: No recursive rollback/cleanup. Created metadata in old root is NOT a newly created project root.

PreferenceCommitStatus.rule: Successful receipt has no Failed state. Selected preference failure uses PartialProjectCreated, retaining definition proof.

DefinitionSaveReceipt.rule: Ok iff all requested S2 steps succeed. No settings/registry/generation mutation. Postcommit projection cannot revoke persistence proof.

fields_or_variants.stage: existing CommitStage; Read for FileSystemPort read/exists/is_file errors

StoreFault.rule: Keep original stage/reason. Read error never implies a verified rollback.

RecoveryInfo.rule: Copy exactly from CommitError::RecoveryRequired; no invented diagnostic paths or version-presence claims.

CodecIssue.rule: No IO; syntax/duplicate/resource checks precede schema dispatch.

CreationFailureCause.rule: RecoveryRequired is deliberately not nested; it has higher-priority top-level classification.

DefinitionStoreError.rule: Local typed HOST data, not new IPC schema. S3 rejects UnauthorizedCaller before S2. No implicit retry/remap/cleanup.

CreationArtifactKind.rule: Exact discriminants; no serialization/IPC contract is added in S2.

invariants.rule: New root/config creation uses exclusive commit Port; no exists/create_dir_all success fallback.
S2 never increments revision; proof/ack refers only to captured immutable snapshot.
Raw digest is exact source bytes; revision is logical. Semantically equal reformat still conflicts against stale raw digest.
Definition committed before later prefs failure remains committed; return partial with proof, never all-unchanged claim.
RecoveryRequired is top-level priority with exact IO diagnostic paths, never ordinary Partial/Storage.
Adoption only adds definition/missing metadata directory; protects ESS/manifest/preferences bytes.
No settings, active binding, UUID registry, Undo or approval-auth mutation. S3 later owner/session gate.
Supported extensions preserved; duplicate/unknown known-schema/unrepresentable content rejected, not discarded.
HOST does not own/delete IO scratch or other files; no recursive cleanup.

save_details: expected_disk_digest must exactly equal binding baseline, otherwise InvalidInput ExpectedDigestMismatch before writes
New root and metadata exclusively created; then definition expectedNone; selected prefs expectedNone; no other file generated
Existing update acquires definition lease, reads raw under lease, compares raw digest before decoding; changed bytes → RevisionConflict even if malformed or different UUID
If digest matches, decode and compare UUID/opened logical revision; UUID mismatch → IdentityConflict, revision mismatch → RevisionConflict
Captured revision may advance by multiple S1 edits; no upper step+1 assumption. Same revision must have identical semantic definition; smaller revision rejected
NoOp is not a new result variant: explicit save may commit identical bytes at same revision, returning a fresh IO transaction receipt. S2 does not force an extra logical revision
Legacy adoption requires Absent baseline and explicit authorized adoption location; only root metadata may already exist; no replacing existing definition
Same-root peer UUID claim allowed; same UUID at another canonical root conflicts before creation/adoption/open install; no move/copy resolution in S2
A read-only open detects stale source if a second exact raw read differs; return RevisionConflict, never mix version/digest
New first-save failure leaves owned artifacts/proof and requires explicit user action; retrying New location against existing root is ExistingTarget. S3 request-ID dedupe/repair are not hidden in S2
open_definition returns Legacy only if definition is NotFound AND trusted existing root still exists and is not a file; disappeared/invalid root → InvalidLocation, not Legacy
After first successful read, any second-read error/change is RevisionConflict; never return digest/content from different reads
Empty selection/session/window context → NotBound before read/mutation. S3 is still responsible for authenticity and current owner membership.
Native CommitError::InvalidPath → InvalidLocation with retained artifacts; if THIS operation already created the root, PartialProjectCreated cause InvalidLocation.

Before constructing commit proof check receipt target equals trusted canonical requested target, committed_digest equals exact encoded requested bytes, previous_digest equals expected baseline and txid is32 lowercase hex. No extra postcommit FS re-read that could misclassify a later external edit.

A contradictory/malformed successful receipt → top-level CommitEvidenceMismatch, retain reported receipt/progress and block further write/binding. Never call it ordinary Storage/rollback and never fabricate IO journal diagnostics. Preferences mismatch retains earlier definition proof. This guards a Port contract violation without changing IO Port.

Preference consistency by location: NewProject requires prepared plan kind exactly matches snapshot preferenceSource; ExistingProject requires Skip write plan but preserves historical snapshot preferenceSource preset/imported-copy; LegacyAdoption requires both Skip plan and snapshot preferenceSource skip.
These location-specific rules prevent overwriting existing preferences on normal definition updates without incorrectly rejecting a saved project that originally chose a preset.
